content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Billings

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a four-year degree with three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma with five years of equivalent experience. Review PMI's education and experience requirements carefully, then gather documentation of your project roles. Billings's major employers across healthcare, energy, construction, and logistics all value certified project managers.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. You'll attend interactive sessions from anywhere in Montana or beyond, learning frameworks, best practices, and exam strategies from active certified practitioners. The course covers all five process groups and is designed to prepare you for exam success.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing the 35 contact hours, submit your formal PMI application online, including your education, experience, and training documentation. Pay the associated examination fee to PMI. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before scheduling your exam appointment.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—including practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to strengthen your readiness. Schedule your computer-based exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. On exam day, demonstrate your project-management knowledge across all five domains tested by PMI.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After earning your PMP, commit to the standard three-year renewal cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, or completing relevant work experience. Renew your credential on PMI's schedule to keep it active and stay current in your field.
